messages.content: ok what is the current state of brain learning

The "zebra" test lessons appear in `learn-events.jsonl` but never made it into `playbook.json` — that whole thread was a diagnostic/test loop (deliberately invoking a fake `zebra` command to test the learning pipeline itself), not real lessons, so it correctly stayed out of the persisted playbook.

**Current state of Brain Learning** (`crs-brain/data/playbook.json` + `learn-events.jsonl`):

**9 active lessons in the Playbook**, all `status: active`, none archived/superseded:

| Category | Count | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| workspace-rule | 4 | index page.json un-editable, no scratch files in worktree, git checkout/reset blocked, `generate-ids` takes positional arg not `--count` |
| design-pattern | 2 | light/dark theme via per-element `bptheme` states, anonymous users have no theme |
| decision-pointer | 1 | anonymous sign-in page is dark by design (Vlad's 2026-07-19 ruling) |
| cli-bug | 1 | use `node` not `python` — python isn't installed on the Windows host |
| platform-gotcha | 1 | `buildprint sync` "Unauthorized" ≠ stale data — check sync status first |

**Provenance:** 7 lessons were migrated in from the old memory system on 2026-07-19T00:21; 2 are freshly learned from a real BP session (`chat fdfec816`) at 02:41.

**Reuse signal:** only 3 of 9 have ever fired again (`hits` 1, 1, 2) — the python→node rule fired twice, the strongest repeat offender so far.

**Test-loop noise:** the `learn-events.jsonl` log also contains ~7 events from a synthetic "zebra" diagnostic used to validate the learning pipeline (learn → save → apply → detect recurrence). Working as intended — a recurrence was correctly flagged once — but that's pipeline self-test, not product knowledge.

No stale/wrong lessons flagged, no `recurred` counts above 0 outside the deliberate zebra test.
